Immunohistochemical analysis showed that there was no serine/threonine-protein kinase B-raf (BRAF)-V600E mutation (Figure 1H).

report.source_text: A follow-up assessment at 9 years showed no recurrence or new lesion (Figure 1J and 1K).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 1-year-old male presented with limp, fever, and difficulty moving the left leg. Initial radiographs showed a radiolucent lesion with periosteal reaction at the left proximal tibia. Histopathological biopsy of the tibial lesion confirmed Langerhans cell histiocytosis with positive immunostaining for CD1a, S-100, and CD207 and absence of BRAF V600E mutation. Initial skeletal survey and brain MRI showed no other lesions. Two months post-curettage, a new osteolytic skull lesion and temporalis soft tissue mass developed, indicating multifocal osseous LCH. Chemotherapy with vincristine and prednisolone was started following the Taiwan Paediatric Oncology Group low-risk protocol. Long-term follow-up at 9 years post-treatment revealed no recurrence or new lesions.
